title: A Atlas for the Regiment
premise: Ulyana Sandoval, a pearl diver's child indentured to the Verrin Trading Company, has spent nineteen years believing history is something that happens to other people, in cities she'll never see. When a half-frozen stranger washes up at the company post carrying letters in the unmistakable handwriting of her father — declared dead a decade ago — Ulyana discovers he faked his drowning to smuggle out proof of the Company's falsified ledgers, and that the Company's enforcers are closing in. As winter locks the river, Ulyana, her ailing mother, and the stranger must decide who takes the last berth on the icebreaker before the river freezes solid, while the Company demands the letters in exchange for cancelling her indenture. In the end, Ulyana sends her mother north with the letters, stays behind to testify before the magistrate, and learns that survival is not the same thing as living — and that the family you choose can outlast the one you were given.
about_author: Edmund Ashgrove is the pen name of a former river-port archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trading-company correspondence before turning to fiction. He writes historical fiction about the people ledgers forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A day in the life of a Company pearl diver: the cold, the quotas, the small economies of kindness among the indentured workers. She patches her mother's cough with traded medicine and tells herself the Company post is the whole world. Emotional beat: weary contentment built on willful blindness.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ice Hole
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The workers pull a half-drowned man from the river — a courier named Davor, clutching a wax-sealed satchel he refuses to surrender even unconscious. When Ulyana sees the handwriting inside, she recognizes her father's slanted letters, the same hand that taught her to write. Emotional beat: the ground tilts; the past is not past.

chapters.title: Letters from a Drowned Man
chapters.summary: Davor's POV. Recovering in the infirmary, he explains: Ulyana's father faked his death ten years ago to smuggle out ledgers proving the Company sold indentured divers' debts to slavers upriver. Davor was his last courier. Emotional beat: grief curdling into fury — her father chose the cause over them.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She and Davor decode the letters: her father is alive at a safehouse two hundred miles north, and the Company auditor arrives within the week hunting the missing pages. Ulyana realizes her own indenture contract is among the forged debts. Emotional beat: the personal made political; history has been happening to her all along.

chapters.title: What the Overseer Knows
chapters.summary: Overseer Brandt's POV. Brandt, who has quietly falsified quotas for years to keep divers alive, is pressured by the auditor to produce results. He suspects Ulyana but hesitates, remembering her father. Emotional beat: a compromised man's conscience — loyalty to the Company warring with loyalty to its people.

chapters.title: Found Family, Fraying Seams
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The indentured divers — old Maren, the twins, quiet Tomas — learn the truth and must choose: report the strangers for reduced sentences, or shelter them. They choose each other. Davor teaches Ulyana the courier's routes. Emotional beat: warmth before the storm; the found family solidifies.

chapters.title: The Auditor's Offer
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The auditor corners Ulyana privately: surrender the letters and her father's location, and the Company cancels her indenture and her mother's debt. He gives her until the icebreaker's last sailing. Emotional beat: temptation with a clean face — survival offered at the price of everyone else.

chapters.title: Ice Breaking
chapters.summary: Davor's POV. The auditor's enforcers raid the barracks; Maren is taken, Tomas is hurt, and Davor is captured protecting the satchel. Brandt, forced to choose, quietly unlocks the boathouse and lets Ulyana go, staying to face the consequences. Emotional beat: sacrifice as proof of loyalty; the cost becomes real.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the frozen dock, one berth remains on the icebreaker. Her mother is dying; Davor is in chains; the letters must reach the magistrate before the Company buries them. Ulyana puts her mother aboard with the letters and turns back to testify herself. Emotional beat: the blurb's terrible choice, made — love expressed as letting go.

chapters.title: An Atlas Drawn by Hand
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, months later. Her testimony, corroborated by the letters, breaks the Company's charter; the divers' debts are voided. Her mother writes from the north — their father received the pages and is coming home. Ulyana, free for the first time, draws a map of the river country for the freed divers. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; history, she now knows, is made by whoever stays to write it down.
